parts.title: Multiple choice — Booking a school trip

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Oakfield Activity Centre, good morning.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: Oh, hello. I'd like to ask about a visit for a school group, please. We're thinking of coming in early June, on the twelfth, if that's possible.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Let me check. The twelfth is fine, yes, although the climbing wall is closed that week for repainting.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: That's a pity. The children were really looking forward to the climbing wall. Could we switch to the canoeing session instead?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Of course. Canoeing is the same price, and it's actually more popular. Just bear in mind children need a signed permission form for any water activity.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: Right, I'll send those out with the letters. How many children can one instructor take?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Twelve. So if you bring twenty-four, we'd assign two instructors, and the whole group can go together.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: And lunch? I remember last time we had to eat outside because the dining hall was fully booked.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The dining hall is available this time — I can reserve it for one o'clock. There's also a picnic area if you'd rather be outdoors, but the hall is booked for you from one until two.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: The hall, please. And do you still charge an entry fee for adults?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Adults are free, yes. The children's fee is six pounds fifty each, and that includes all equipment.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: Perfect. I'll confirm by email this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Hi there, are you looking for anything in particular today?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes — a laptop for university. I need something light enough to carry every day, and the battery has to last through a full day of lectures.

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Then I'd avoid the Stream 15. It's powerful, but it weighs over two kilos and the battery manages about five hours. It's really aimed at gamers.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Okay, not that one. What about this silver one here?

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: The Feather 13? That's our lightest model — just over a kilo — and the battery lasts eleven hours. The only downside is the storage: a hundred and twenty-eight gigabytes, which is a bit tight if you keep a lot of videos.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: I mostly write essays and stream films, so that's probably fine. Does it have a good screen for long study sessions?

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: It does, but to be honest, if screen comfort matters most I'd look at the Vision 14. It's a little heavier, at one and a half kilos, and the battery is ten hours, but the display is much easier on the eyes.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Hmm. The Feather is cheaper, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Actually no — the Feather is our premium model. The Vision is on special offer this month, so it's a hundred pounds less.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Interesting. And can I add extra memory to the Vision later?

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: You can, yes — the memory is user-upgradable, unlike the Feather where it's fixed. I'd say the Vision is the better fit for a student.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: I think you're right. I'll take the Vision 14.

lines.speaker: Librarian
lines.text: Thanks for coming, everyone. The library is reviewing its services, and I'd like to hear what you actually use.

lines.speaker: Student A
lines.text: I mainly come for the group study rooms. They're almost always full, though — we've started booking days in advance.

lines.speaker: Student B
lines.text: For me it's the online journals. I work part-time, so I do most of my reading at home late at night.

lines.speaker: Librarian
lines.text: So the study rooms and the digital collections. Anyone else?

lines.speaker: Student C
lines.text: The printing service, definitely. It's cheap and the machines almost never break, which is more than I can say for the ones in town.

lines.speaker: Student B
lines.text: Oh, and the borrowing scheme for laptops — I used that last term when mine needed repairing.

lines.speaker: Librarian
lines.text: Right. And which areas could we improve? Let's each name two things.

lines.speaker: Student A
lines.text: Opening hours, first. Closing at eight means night-before-exam students have nowhere to go. And the café — it's fine, but the coffee machine is broken half the time.

lines.speaker: Student C
lines.text: I'd say the noise in the silent area. People treat it like a common room. That, and there are never enough power sockets.

lines.speaker: Librarian
lines.text: Thank you — opening hours, café, noise and sockets. We'll take these to the next planning meeting.

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: Welcome to the housing advice line. How can I help today?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: We're moving to the city next month and we've never rented through an agency before. What should we prepare?

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: The two documents you'll definitely need are proof of income, usually three recent payslips, and photo identification. A reference from a previous landlord helps a lot as well.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: And how much should we expect to pay before we move in?

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: Normally one month's rent in advance plus a deposit equal to one month's rent. Some agencies also charge an administration fee, but that's becoming less common.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: What about viewing a property? We've both got jobs, so evenings are easiest for us.

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: Most agencies offer evening viewings, yes. I'd book two or three on the same evening and take notes, because it's easy to confuse properties afterwards. Check the water pressure and whether the windows open properly.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Useful. And the contract — anything we should look out for?

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: Two things: how long the fixed term is, and the notice period. Six-month terms are standard, and notice is usually one month. If there's a break clause, make sure you understand it.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Brilliant, thank you. That's very clear.

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: So let's match each of you with the right evening course. First, Ana — you said you wanted something creative but also practical?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes, I'd love to be able to make things. I was thinking pottery, but the beginner class is full.

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: Then take woodwork. It's very hands-on, and the tutor says beginners pick it up quickly.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I need something for my job, honestly. I write reports but I'm slow at typing, and my presentations look terrible.

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: The computer skills course covers exactly that — documents and slides, one evening a week.

lines.speaker: Cara
lines.text: For me it's more about health. I sit at a desk all day, and my back is starting to complain.

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: We have a yoga class on Tuesdays. It's gentle and specifically aimed at office workers.

lines.speaker: Dan
lines.text: I'd like to cook properly instead of heating things up. Nothing too fancy.

lines.speaker: Adviser
lines.text: The basic cookery course, then. You start with soups and simple sauces, and by the end you can manage a full dinner.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Right, let's settle the details of the office move. The new floor is smaller, so we need to decide what happens to the furniture.

lines.speaker: Ella
lines.text: I think we should keep the big meeting table. It's the only place the whole team can sit together, and clients use it too.

lines.speaker: Farid
lines.text: The old filing cabinets, though — nobody uses them any more. Everything's digital now, so they can go to recycling.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: What about the plants? I'll volunteer to water them if we keep them, because they make the office feel much less like a box.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: And the notice board?

lines.speaker: Farid
lines.text: That should stay. It's where we post the health and safety information — we're legally required to display it somewhere.

lines.speaker: Ella
lines.text: The spare monitors can be sold, surely? There are at least six of them in the cupboard and we never use them.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Fine. Table and board stay, cabinets recycled, monitors sold, and Grace takes charge of the plants.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Welcome to Riverside Park. You've come in through the main gate at the south end, and the path straight ahead of you runs north towards the lake in the centre of the park.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: If you look to your left, just before the lake, you'll see the children's playground — you can't miss the climbing frames.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: On the opposite side of the path, to the east, is the café, which is open until six. It's right next to the path, so it's handy for a stop on the way back.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Beyond the lake, on the far side, is the rose garden. In June it's spectacular, and there are benches all around it.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: And if you fancy going out on the water, the boat hire hut is on the lake's eastern shore — it's the small building with the blue roof.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: OK, this is your campus tour. You came in through the main entrance, and the building straight in front of you is reception — that's where you collect your student card.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: To the right of reception, on the east side, is the library. It's open until ten on weekdays.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: If you carry on further east, right to the edge of the campus, you'll come to the sports hall. That's the newest building here.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: On the other side of reception, to the west, is the science block. The labs are on the top floor.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: And the canteen is just behind the science block, on its north side. It's cheaper than anywhere in town, honestly.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Oh, and if you drove, the car park is outside the west edge of the campus, near the science block.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Right, you've just come out of the station. The main road runs straight ahead, north, all the way to the clock tower in the middle of the town.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: As you walk up, the post office is on your left, on the west side of the road. It's directly opposite the bank.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: The bank is on the right-hand side, so on the east. If you need cash, that's where the only machine in town is.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Keep walking past the bank and the road bends to the right at the corner. The museum is just around that corner, on your right.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Back near the post office, the pharmacy is right next door to it, on the north side. You can't get prescriptions anywhere else on a Sunday.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: And if you go all the way to the clock tower, the park is just beyond it, to the north. It's a good place to sit for ten minutes.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Welcome! You've just come through the entrance at the south end. Follow the path north and you'll pass the shop first, on the west side — it sells everything from milk to postcards.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Opposite the shop, on the east side, is the reception office. That's where you pick up your key cards and towels.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Further up, the path splits in two. If you take the left-hand fork, heading west, you'll reach the swimming pool. It opens at seven in the morning.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: The right-hand fork, to the east, takes you to the restaurant. Breakfast is served there from eight to ten.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Straight ahead between the two forks, just north of where the path splits, is the children's club. It runs activities from nine until four.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: And your cabins are along the north edge of the camp, behind the children's club.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: Today we're looking at how a water filter jug works. Let's go through its parts from the top down.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: At the very top is the lid, which has a small spout so you can pour without removing it.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: Under the lid is the upper funnel. That's where you pour the tap water in — it holds about one litre at a time.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: Inside the funnel sits the cartridge. This is the part that actually removes impurities, and it should be replaced every four weeks.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: The filtered water then collects in the chamber below the funnel. The clear section lets you see how much you have left.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: And finally, attached to the side of the jug is the handle, which is wide enough to grip even when the jug is full.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: Let's run through the main parts of the bike before your first ride. Starting at the front: those are the handlebars, which you use for steering.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: Below the handlebars is the front wheel. Make sure the tyre is firm before every ride — squeeze it with your thumb.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: In the middle of the frame is the saddle. That's the seat, and we'll adjust its height before we set off.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: Behind the saddle is the rear wheel. The brake lever on the right handlebar controls it.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: Now the pedals, down between the two wheels. Pushing them turns the chain, which runs around the gears at the back.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: If the chain ever comes off, stop pedalling immediately and let me know.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Westfield College, enrolments.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Hello, I'd like to enrol on the photography course that starts in September, please.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Of course. Can I take your full name?

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: It's Daniel Okonkwo. That's O-K-O-N-K-W-O.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Thank you. And your date of birth?

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: The fourteenth of March, nineteen ninety-eight.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Great. The course fee is one hundred and eighty-five pounds, which includes all materials except the memory card.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Fine. Do you need my phone number?

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Please. And an email for the confirmation.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: The number is oh seven eight four six, double five, two one three. And my email is daniel dot okonkwo at mail dot com.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: 07846 55213, daniel.okonkwo@mail.com. The course runs on Tuesday evenings, starting on the ninth of September, in room fourteen of the arts block.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Tuesdays work well. How do I pay?

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: You can pay by card now, or in person before the first session. A receipt will be emailed to you with the joining instructions.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: I'll pay now by card, thanks.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The Harbour Hotel, how may I help?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: I'd like to book a room for two nights, from the twenty-fifth of August, please.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Let me look. We have a standard double at eighty-six pounds a night, or a sea-view room at one hundred and ten.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: The standard double is fine. Is breakfast included?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: It isn't, I'm afraid, but guests get ten per cent off at the café next door with their room key.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Understood. My name is Helen Marsh — M-A-R-S-H.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Thank you. Could I take a contact number?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Sure, it's oh one one three, seven nine four, double eight six two.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: 0113 794 8862. And what time will you arrive on the twenty-fifth?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Around four in the afternoon. Oh, and could I have a room on a high floor if possible?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: I've noted that. The reference for your booking is HB two nine seven one. Check-in is from three o'clock.
